name: Murf
summary: AI voiceover generation for explainers, courses and product video.
best_for: creators, trainers and product teams that need studio-quality voiceovers in many languages without booking voice actors — explainers, courses, product videos
skip_if: you need real emotional acting range for premium brand work (humans still win), or your volume is tiny enough that free TTS built into your video tool suffices
honest_knock: The meter is generation hours per YEAR, not per month — 24 hours sounds generous until you count retakes, and regenerating a script three times bills three times. Voice quality is genuinely strong, but the honest test for any TTS is your specific language, names and jargon: generate your hardest paragraph in the trial before subscribing, because demo voices always sound better than your edge cases.

pricing.plans_source: summarised from pricing.notes; every plan name and amount appears verbatim in those notes
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-03 in a browser; the page renders client-side and opens on annual billing, so check which column you are reading) Studio plans: Free $0 for 10 projects, 10 minutes of voice generation and one editor, with no downloads and no commercial rights. Creator $19/mo billed annually ($228 a year): 100 projects, 24 hours of voice generation a year, 1 editor, all 200+ voices, unlimited downloads and commercial rights. Business $66/mo billed annually ($792 a year): 500 projects, 96 hours of generation a year, business licence, PowerPoint integration and audio-to-text. Enterprise is custom and is where voice cloning, SSO and AI translation sit. Annual billing is advertised as saving 33%. Dub and the API are separate products with their own pricing — the API tab of the pricing page meters by characters, not hours: $0.01 per 1,000 characters on the Falcon model and $0.03 on the studio-quality model, with $10 of free credit a month on the API trial and purchased credit that does not expire. The Studio ladder on the page is Free, Creator, Business and Enterprise; there is no Growth plan, and Creator and Business are capped at one editor seat each, so a second person means Enterprise.
